topic.title: Review Task States and Review Status
topic.shortdesc: This topic explains the states a review task can have.

body.p: The states of a review task depend on the type of review task because Project Review Tasks and Independent Review Tasks have different workflows. Transitioning the task from one state to another is done by actions made by a task owner. The review status is a rendering of the task state for a particular review task role. For the owner the review status is the same as the task state, but for the reviewer the review status reflects only the states that are relevant for that role.

section.title: Review status versus review task state
section.p: The task state generates a review status information that is presented to a collaborator. The review status depends both on the task state and on the role of the collaborator. The review status matches in general the state of the task, but in some cases the actual state is not relevant for a specific role, so the review status presents the relevant information for that role instead of the actual state. More specific, a will see the review status as Review closed for a task that is in the Review closed state or in follow-up states, that are not relevant for the reviewers, because from their point of view those states are equivalent to the Review closed state.

section.title: Project Review Tasks states
section.p:
A Project Review Tasks can be in one of the following states: In review, Review closed, Integrating, or Integrated. The review status information associated to these states is presented in the following table: How task state is rendered as review status based on the role
Task state In review Review closed Integrating Integrated
Owner review status In review Review closed Integrating Integrated
Reviewer review status In review Review closed Review closed Review closed
Here there are details about each state:

li.p: In review - This is the initial state for newly created review tasks. Tasks remain in this state until a task owner closes the review. Both reviewers and task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. To close the review a task owner can use the Close review button, and the task will transition to the Review closed state.

Review closed - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Close Review button. Only task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for reviewers. Task owners can reopen the task using the Reopen Review button, and its state returns to In review or they can start the integration process to merge the task changes into the original content using the Start integration button. Only one owner will be able to use the Start integration action, to keep the integration responsibility to a single person.

Integrating - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Start Integrating button to integrate the task changes into the project. Only the task owner who started the integration can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for all other collaborators. From this state the owner that handles the integration can use Cancel integration to return to the Review closed state, or finalize the integration and merge the changes into the original project content using the Finish integration button.

Integrated - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Finish Integration button after the integration is complete. Task files are read-only for all participants. An integrated review task can no longer be reopened.

p.note: The review status presented to reviewers for the Integrating and Integrated is Review closed, because from the reviewers point of view these states are equivalent to the Review closed state.

section.title: Independent Review Tasks states
section.p: An Independent Review Tasks can be in one of the following states: In review, Review closed, or Integrated.

table.title: How task state is rendered as review status based on the role

li.p: In review - This is the initial state for newly created review tasks. Tasks remain in this state until a task owner closes the review. Both reviewers and task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. To close the review a task owner can use the Close review button, and the task will transition to the Review closed state.

Review closed - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Close Review button. Only task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for reviewers. Task owners can reopen the task using the Reopen Review button, and its state returns to In review, or they can mark that they integrated the content of the task using the Mark as integrated button, and the task will transition to the Integrated state,

Integrated - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Mark as integrated button on a closed task to mark that the content of the task was integrated and it is not needed anymore. In this state, task files are read-only for all participants and the task is visible only to the task owners. Using the Mark as not integrated button allows owners to transition the task back to the Review closed state.
